[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Optimization Algorithms in Machine Learning: SGD, Adam, and RMSprop"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Optimization algorithms are the engine of machine learning models. They dictate how the model updates its parameters (weights and biases) based on the computed gradients of the loss function, aiming to minimize error as efficiently as possible."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Standard Gradient Descent calculates the gradient of the objective function for the entire dataset, which is computationally expensive for large datasets. Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) addresses this by updating parameters using only a single sample or a small mini-batch at each iteration."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pros: Computationally efficient, handles large datasets well, and the noise in parameter updates can help escape local minima."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cons: Updates can be noisy and oscillate wildly around the global minimum, making convergence slow or erratic."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.optim as optim

# Defining a simple model and SGD optimizer
model = torch.nn.Linear(10, 1)
optimizer = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01, momentum=0.9)"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. RMSprop (Root Mean Square Propagation)"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"RMSprop is an adaptive learning rate method designed to resolve the radically diminishing learning rates of standard gradient descent variants. It divides the learning rate by an exponentially decaying average of squared gradients."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mechanics: Keeps a moving average of squared gradients and normalizes the gradient update, reducing oscillations in high-curvature directions."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Implementing RMSprop in PyTorch
optimizer = optim.RMSprop(model.parameters(), lr=0.001, alpha=0.99)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Adam (Adaptive Moment Estimation)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Adam is currently the most popular optimization algorithm in deep learning. It combines the best properties of both AdaGrad and RMSprop. Adam calculates adaptive learning rates for each parameter by storing both the exponentially decaying average of past gradients (first moment / mean) and past squared gradients (second moment / uncentered variance)."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"First Moment (Mean): Tracks the direction of gradients (momentum)."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Second Moment (Variance): Tracks the magnitude of gradients (scaling)."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"# Implementing Adam in PyTorch
optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001, betas=(0.9, 0.999), eps=1e-8)"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion and Best Practices"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"While Adam is typically the default choice for most deep learning tasks due to its fast convergence and robustness, SGD with momentum is still widely preferred in computer vision domains where it often generalizes better to test data. Always experiment with learning rate schedules and different optimizers to find the optimal configuration for your specific architecture."}]
